items.title: Some users may be delayed when sending or receiving email in Exchange Online
items.summary: Affected users may see delays of up to 20 minutes when sending or receiving email.

provider.impact:
Affected users may see delays of up to 20 minutes when sending or receiving email.

Scope of impact: Any user served by the affected infrastructure may be impacted.

items.title: Action required: decide how long anonymous sharing links should last
items.summary:
Microsoft is changing the default expiration for anonymous sharing links in SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Links created before the change keep working until their new expiration date unless an administrator sets a policy of their own.
How this will affect your organization: Anonymous links will stop working sooner than they do today when no policy is set.
What you need to do to prepare: Review the sharing settings in the SharePoint admin center, decide whether to keep the new default or set your own, and tell the teams that rely on long-lived links.

items.title: Retirement: basic authentication for SMTP client submission in Exchange Online
items.summary:
Basic authentication for SMTP client submission is being retired. Devices and applications that still send mail with a username and password will need to move to modern authentication.
How this will affect your organization: Scanners, instruments and older applications that submit mail directly may stop sending.
What you need to do to prepare: List the devices that submit mail through your tenant, check which of them support modern authentication, and plan a replacement for the rest.

items.title: A redesigned meeting recap is coming to Microsoft Teams
items.summary:
Meeting recaps in Microsoft Teams are getting a new layout that puts decisions and follow-up items first. The change rolls out to all users without any administrator action.
How this will affect your organization: People will see the new layout the next time they open a recap.
What you need to do to prepare: Nothing is required. You may want to tell your help desk about the new layout.

definition.title: Inactive accounts
definition.description: Every account and how long it has gone without signing in, from Microsoft's last sign-in dates. Pick a range or sort by days.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Days since the last successful sign-in. With no success on record, since the last attempt; with no sign-in at all, since the account was created.

columns.label: Last successful sign-in
columns.help: Interactive or background. Microsoft has recorded this since 1 December 2023.

columns.label: Last interactive attempt
columns.help: The last time the person signed in themselves, successfully or not.

columns.label: Last background attempt
columns.help: The last time an app signed in for the person, successfully or not.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 in the tenant, which Microsoft requires for sign-in dates.
A role that can read sign-in activity, such as Reports Reader, Security Reader or Global Reader.

notes: Days count from the last successful sign-in, interactive or background. Microsoft has recorded successful sign-ins only since 1 December 2023, so an account with none since then is counted from its last attempt, which can only make it look more recent.
Attempts, no success: accounts that tried to sign in after December 2023 with no successful sign-in on record. Check them for a broken account or someone guessing passwords.
Never signed in means Microsoft has no sign-in on record. Its records start in April 2020, so these accounts are counted from creation or April 2020, whichever is later.
Shared mailboxes, rooms and equipment are accounts too and normally never sign in.

definition.title: Licenses to reclaim
definition.description: Licensed accounts that are disabled or have not signed in for 30 days or more, and how each license was assigned.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Counted the same way as the Inactive accounts audit. Empty when last sign-in dates could not be read.

columns.label: Assigned
columns.help: A license assigned by a group comes back if you remove it directly. Remove the account from the group instead.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: Without sign-in dates (AuditLog.Read.All with Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2), only disabled accounts are listed.

notes: By product: Microsoft 365 Business Premium 11, Microsoft Power Automate Free 6, Exchange Online (Plan 1) 2.
Microsoft does not report prices, so Prism365 counts seats, not cost.

definition.title: MFA registration
definition.description: Who has registered a strong sign-in method and who has not, with the admins who rely on phone or text codes. From Microsoft's authentication methods report.

columns.label: MFA registered
columns.help: Microsoft's definition: at least one strong method your authentication methods policy allows is registered.

columns.label: Domain
columns.help: The part of the sign-in name after the @. Filter by it to look at one domain without changing the audit scope.

requirements: A role such as Reports Reader, Security Reader, Security Administrator or Global Reader.

notes: Microsoft's report leaves out disabled accounts.
Registered is not the same as required. Conditional Access or security defaults decide whether a sign-in asks for MFA.
Phone or text only: the strongest method registered is a text message or call, which phishing and SIM swaps can defeat. Move these accounts, admins first, to the Authenticator app or a passkey.
Microsoft refreshes this report on its own schedule. Report updated shows when each row was refreshed.

definition.title: Guest accounts
definition.description: External guests in the tenant: invitations never accepted, guests who never signed in, and guests who have gone quiet.

columns.label: Invited
columns.help: When the guest account was created, which is when the invitation was sent.

columns.label: Inactive for
columns.help: Counted the same way as the Inactive accounts audit. Empty when last sign-in dates could not be read.

requirements: Sign-in dates need AuditLog.Read.All and Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2. Without them, only invitation states are shown.

notes: Every guest here can sign in to whatever was shared with it until the account is disabled or removed.

definition.title: License capacity
definition.description: Each product the tenant subscribes to: seats bought, assigned and free, and subscriptions that have expired or been suspended.

columns.label: In grace period
columns.help: Seats on an expired subscription that can still be assigned until it is renewed or suspended.

columns.label: Available
columns.help: Active and grace-period seats not assigned to anyone. Negative means more are assigned than owned.

requirements: A role that can read subscriptions, such as Directory Readers, Global Reader or License Administrator.

notes: Needs attention: no seats left to assign, more assigned than owned, or a subscription that has expired, been suspended or been locked out.
Products with 10,000 seats or more are usually free or self-service sign-up products, so their seats are not counted as unassigned.
Microsoft does not report prices or renewal dates here, so Prism365 shows seats only.
